context_quotes: The Seebeck coefficient increases sharply while the electrical conductivity and thermal diffusivity drops.
Such behavior has previously been attributed to critical phenomena under the assumption of a continuous phase transition.
records.conditions: Prior interpretation assumes a continuous phase transition; challenged by the present work.

records.subject: Phase diagram consistent with a first-order transition
records.quote: Using the phase diagram that is consistent with a first order transition, we show that the observed transport properties and heat capacity curves can be accounted for and modeled with good agreement.
records.conditions: Good agreement using a phase diagram consistent with a first-order transition.

records.subject: Universal approximants for a single mobility edge
records.quote: The electronic thermoelectric coefficients are analyzed in the vicinity of one and two Anderson localization thresholds in three dimensions.
context_quotes: For a single mobility edge, we correct and extend previous studies and find universal approximants which allow us to deduce the critical exponent for the zero-temperature conductivity from thermoelectric measurements.
records.conditions: From thermoelectric measurements; analysis near a single Anderson mobility edge in three dimensions.

records.subject: Insulating side below the zero-temperature localization threshold
records.quote: The electronic thermoelectric coefficients are analyzed in the vicinity of one and two Anderson localization thresholds in three dimensions.
context_quotes: For a single mobility edge, we correct and extend previous studies and find universal approximants which allow us to deduce the critical exponent for the zero-temperature conductivity from thermoelectric measurements.

In particular, we find that at nonzero low temperatures the Seebeck coefficient and the thermoelectric efficiency can be very large on the insulating side, for chemical potentials below the (zero-temperature) localization threshold.
records.conditions: Nonzero low temperatures; chemical potential below the zero-temperature threshold; single-edge analysis in three dimensions.

records.subject: Decreasing system size
records.quote: The electronic thermoelectric coefficients are analyzed in the vicinity of one and two Anderson localization thresholds in three dimensions.
context_quotes: Next, the thermoelectric coefficients are shown to have interesting dependences on the system size.

While the Seebeck coefficient decreases with decreasing size, the figure of merit first decreases but then increases, while the Wiedemann-Franz ratio first increases but then decreases as the size decreases.
records.conditions: Finite-size dependence in the three-dimensional Anderson-localization analysis.
